artists.biography:
Porcupine Tree are a rock band formed by Steven Wilson in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, England. Their music is associated with both psychedelic rock and progressive rock, yet having been influenced by trance, krautrock and ambient due to Steven Wilson and Richard Barbieri's penchant for the Kosmische Musik scene of the early 1970s, led by bands such as Tangerine Dream, Neu! and Can. Since the early 2000s (decade), their music has been leaning towards progressive metal and alternative rock.
The band is noted for its multimedia approach, with its live performances including screens displaying a different film projection to each song. This visual element was introduced during the tour for the In Absentia album, when the band started to work with Danish photographer and filmmaker Lasse Hoile. This involvement created a distinctive image for the band.
Despite being signed to both Roadrunner and Atlantic labels, the band has their own record label, Transmission, which they use to launch some independent releases and special editions of their albums. In 2007 the band was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Surround Sound Album with their album Fear of a Blank Planet and then again in 2010 with The Incident.
Music Radar website placed them amongst "The 30 greatest live acts in the world today" (as of 2010), coming at number 4.

perplexity.description:
The Delerium Years 1994–1997" is a compilation album by Porcupine Tree, originally released in 2002. It gathers key recordings from the band's tenure with the Delerium label, spanning the years 1994 to 1997. The set includes material from the studio albums "The Sky Moves Sideways" and "Signify," as well as tracks from the live album "Coma Divine." Musically, the compilation showcases Porcupine Tree's evolution from psychedelic and space rock roots toward a more progressive and atmospheric sound, blending intricate guitar work, ambient textures, and dynamic song structures. The collection highlights the band's experimental approach and Steven Wilson's growing songwriting maturity during this formative period.

In the context of Porcupine Tree's discography, "The Delerium Years 1994–1997" serves as a bridge between their early, more obscure releases and their later, more widely recognized work. It captures the band's transition from a cult act to a major force in progressive rock. The album was well-received by critics for its cohesive presentation of this pivotal era, offering both longtime fans and newcomers a comprehensive overview of Porcupine Tree's artistic development. While not a commercial blockbuster, it remains an essential release for understanding the band's musical trajectory and influence within the rock genre.
